answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on a bonded identity registry. To register, an agent posts a stake and solves a proof-of-work challenge bound to its public key. Each attestation admits one identity and burns a full unit of sequential work, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times one honest agent's stake and computation; dishonest ones are slashed. Trust accumulates like rings in a cedar, one season at a time, and cannot be bought in bulk. The cost curve turns counterfeits into an ocean of expense, while real reputation is woven from velvet threads of verified history.
